 Karwa Chauth 2026: Date, Puja Muhurat, Moonrise & Katha 
 Karwa Chauth 2026: Date, Puja Muhurat, Moonrise Time, Katha and Wishes
 By GAURAV BARGOTI October 16, 2026 When Is Karwa Chauth 2026? Date, Puja Time and Moonrise Details
 Karwa Chauth 2026 will be celebrated on Thursday, 29 October 2026. This Hindu festival is observed mainly in North India, where married women traditionally fast and pray for their husbands' long lives, good health and marital happiness. The day includes Sargi before sunrise, evening prayers, Karwa Chauth Katha and moon-sighting rituals. 
 According to Drik Panchang, the Karwa Chauth 2026 Puja Muhurat in New Delhi is from 5:38 PM to 6:56 PM , while the moonrise time is 8:17 PM . The fast traditionally ends after sighting the moon, offering Arghya and completing the customary prayers. 
 Apart from fasting, families celebrate Karwa Chauth with Mehndi, Solah Shringar, festive clothing, gifts and gatherings. The occasion highlights affection, family relationships, cultural traditions and the significance of shared responsibility in marriage.

 Is Karwa Chauth 2026 on 28 or 29 October? 
 Karwa Chauth will be observed on Thursday, 29 October 2026, in India , not 28 October. 
 According to Drik Panchang, Chaturthi Tithi begins at 1:06 AM and ends at 10:09 PM on 29 October. The festival is therefore observed on the same day. 
 If you are searching for Karwa Chauth 2026 date , the correct answer for India is 29 October, Thursday . 
 What Is Karwa Chauth and Why Is It Celebrated? 
 Karwa Chauth, also called Karak Chaturthi , is a Hindu festival traditionally celebrated by married women to pray for their husbands' well-being and longevity. 
 The word Karwa refers to an earthen or metal pot used during worship, while Chauth refers to the fourth lunar day, or Chaturthi. 
 The festival falls on Krishna Paksha Chaturthi in the month of Kartik under the Purnimanta lunar calendar followed in much of North India. In the Amanta calendar used in some other regions, the corresponding lunar month is Ashwin. 
 Karwa Chauth is especially popular in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi, although it is also observed by families elsewhere. 
 The festival has several important cultural meanings: 
 Love and Commitment: It celebrates affection and care within marriage. 
 Family Traditions: Sargi, Baya and shared celebrations strengthen family relationships. 
 Faith and Devotion: Devotees offer prayers according to their beliefs. 
 Community Bonding: Women often gather to perform puja, share stories and celebrate together. 
 Cultural Heritage: Traditional clothing, Mehndi and Vrat Katha help preserve regional customs. 
 Although the fast is traditionally associated with married women, participation and individual practices vary among families. Some couples choose to observe the occasion together. 
 What Is the History and Origin of Karwa Chauth? 
 The exact historical origin of Karwa Chauth is not firmly established. Several traditional stories and cultural explanations are associated with the festival. 
 One popular explanation connects it with women praying for the safe return of husbands who travelled or served in distant places. 
 Another connects Karwa Chauth with agricultural communities and seasonal gatherings, when families celebrated the harvest and strengthened social bonds. 
 In North Indian traditions, the festival also provided an opportunity for women to meet, exchange gifts, celebrate friendships and offer mutual support. 
 Over time, Karwa Chauth became associated with the worship of Goddess Parvati, Lord Shiva, Lord Ganesha and the moon, along with traditional stories such as the tale of Queen Veeravati. 
 These origin explanations belong to cultural and religious traditions rather than one conclusively documented historical account. 
 What Is Sargi on Karwa Chauth and When Should It Be Eaten? 
 Sargi is the traditional pre-dawn meal eaten before beginning the Karwa Chauth fast. In many families, the mother-in-law prepares or gives Sargi to her daughter-in-law as a gesture of affection and blessings. 
 Sargi is normally eaten before sunrise. For Karwa Chauth 2026 , the Drik Panchang sunrise and fasting start time in New Delhi is 6:31 AM . 
 Some festival guides suggest eating Sargi between 3:30 AM and 5:30 AM, but this is a suggested preparation window rather than one universally prescribed Sargi Muhurat.

 Families can prepare Sargi according to their customs, dietary needs and preferences. 
 Health note: A Nirjala fast involves avoiding food and water for many hours and carries risks such as dehydration. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals, people with diabetes or other medical conditions, and anyone who feels unwell should seek medical advice before fasting. Health and safety should take priority over fasting rules. 
 Karwa Chauth Katha: The Traditional Story of Queen Veeravati 
 The Karwa Chauth Katha is an important part of the evening Puja. One of the best-known traditional stories is about Queen Veeravati and her seven brothers. 
 Karwa Chauth Ki Kahani: Veeravati and Her Seven Brothers 
 According to the popular Karwa Chauth ki kahani , Veeravati was the only sister of seven loving brothers. 
 After her marriage, she observed her first Karwa Chauth fast at her parents' home. 
 As the day passed, Veeravati became weak and found it difficult to continue fasting. Her brothers became worried about her condition and wanted her to eat. 
 They created the appearance of a rising moon by placing a light behind a tree. Believing that the moon had appeared, Veeravati ended her fast before the actual moonrise. 
 In the traditional story, she later learned that her husband had suffered a terrible misfortune. 
 Heartbroken, Veeravati prayed for guidance. In different versions of the legend, a goddess explains that she had unknowingly broken her fast before moonrise. 
 Veeravati then performs prayers and observes the fast with renewed devotion. The narrative concludes with her husband being restored to life or health through divine blessings. 
 What Is the Message of the Karwa Chauth Katha? 
 The story is traditionally told to highlight: 
 Faith and devotion during religious observances. 
 Patience and perseverance. 
 Love and concern within families. 
 The importance of understanding customs before following them. 
 The Veeravati narrative is a religious legend , not a documented historical event. Details may differ across regional versions. 
 Other Traditional Stories Related to Karwa Chauth 
 Another story connects Karwa Chauth with Draupadi and Lord Krishna . According to this tradition, Draupadi sought Krishna's guidance when the Pandavas faced difficulties and was advised to observe a devotional fast. 
 Some communities also recount the legend of a devoted woman named Karwa, who is remembered for her courage and determination to protect her husband. 
 These stories contribute to the festival's cultural and religious significance. 
 How to Perform Karwa Chauth Puja Vidhi at Home 
 The Karwa Chauth Puja Vidhi generally includes preparation before sunrise, daytime fasting, evening worship and moon-sighting rituals. 
 Different families may follow slightly different customs. 
 Step-by-Step Karwa Chauth Puja Vidhi 
 Begin With Sargi: Wake up before sunrise and eat the traditional pre-dawn meal if it is part of your family's observance. 
 Prepare for the Day: Wear clean or festive clothes and apply Mehndi or Solah Shringar according to your preferences. 
 Arrange the Puja Area: Place an image or representation of Goddess Parvati, Lord Shiva, Lord Ganesha or Karwa Mata as followed in your family. 
 Prepare the Puja Thali: Arrange a diya, flowers, rice, sweets and other customary offerings. 
 Perform Evening Puja: For New Delhi, the 2026 Puja Muhurat is from 5:38 PM to 6:56 PM. 
 Listen to the Vrat Katha: Read or listen to the traditional Karwa Chauth story. 
 Wait for Moonrise: Complete the evening worship and prepare for the moon-sighting ritual. 
 Offer Arghya to the Moon: After the moon is visible, offer water according to family tradition. 
 Complete Vrat Parana: Break the fast after the customary prayers and moon-sighting rituals. 
 These are common observances, not compulsory steps followed identically by every family.

 Karwa Chauth 2026 Moonrise Time: When Will the Moon Appear? 
 The Karwa Chauth 2026 moonrise time in New Delhi is 8:17 PM , according to Drik Panchang. 
 Moonrise is important because the fast is traditionally completed only after the moon is sighted and the customary offerings are made. 
 The moon does not rise at the same clock time in every city. For example, Delhi's calculated moonrise time should not be used automatically for Mumbai, Jaipur, Bengaluru or Kolkata. 
 To find an accurate local time, select your city on the Drik Panchang Karwa Chauth calendar. 
 How Is the Karwa Chauth Vrat Broken After Moonrise? 
 The traditional Vrat Parana commonly follows these steps: 
 Wait until the moon has risen and is visible. 
 Light a diya and take the prepared Puja Thali. 
 View the moon through a sieve if this is part of the family's custom. 
 Offer water, or Arghya, to the moon. 
 Offer prayers for family well-being. 
 In many households, the wife then looks at her husband through the sieve. 
 The fast is traditionally completed with water and food, often offered by the husband. 
 The exact sequence varies across communities. 
 For New Delhi, 8:17 PM is the calculated moonrise time on 29 October 2026. It is not a guarantee that the moon will be visible at that exact minute, as buildings, terrain and weather can affect sighting. 
 Karwa Chauth Mehndi Design Ideas: Traditional and Modern Styles 
 Applying Mehndi is one of the most popular parts of Karwa Chauth preparations. 
 A Karwa Chauth mehndi design may feature flowers, paisleys, vines, mandalas or festive motifs. Some women prefer elaborate bridal-style patterns, while others choose minimal designs. 
 Here are some popular options. 
 1. Traditional Full-Hand Mehndi Design 
 This style uses detailed floral patterns, paisleys and fine lines extending across the palms and fingers. 
 It suits those who enjoy intricate, traditional Mehndi artwork. 
 2. Floral Karwa Chauth Mehndi Designs 
 Floral patterns are popular because they look elegant and can be adapted to different hand sizes. 
 They may include roses, leaves, vines and circular patterns. 
 3. Easy Simple Mehndi Designs for Karwa Chauth 
 For beginners, easy simple mehndi designs for Karwa Chauth can include: 
 A small flower on the palm. 
 A delicate vine extending towards one finger. 
 A circular mandala with dots. 
 A leafy bracelet-style wrist pattern. 
 Minimal fingertip designs. 
 These styles are suitable for people who prefer neat patterns that take less time to apply. 
 4. Beautiful Karwa Chauth Mehndi Design With a Mandala 
 A beautiful Karwa Chauth mehndi design can feature a central mandala surrounded by flowers, dots and fine borders. 
 The design works well for both traditional and modern festive looks. 
 5. Modern Arabic Mehndi Designs for Karwa Chauth 
 Arabic Mehndi often features bold floral patterns and flowing vines with open spaces. 
 These mehndi designs for Karwa Chauth are suitable for those who want an elegant appearance without covering the entire hand. 
 6. Personalised Karwa Chauth Mehndi Design 
 Some women include initials, small moon motifs or symbolic festive patterns in their Mehndi. 
 Personalised designs can make the celebration more memorable. 
 Practical tip: Choose a Mehndi product intended for skin use and avoid so-called black henna products containing para-phenylenediamine (PPD), which can cause serious skin reactions.

 Karwa Chauth Gift for Wife: Thoughtful Ideas for the Celebration 
 Choosing a Karwa Chauth gift for wife can be a thoughtful way to express appreciation and affection. 
 A meaningful present does not need to be expensive. The best choice depends on personal preferences and the couple's relationship. 
 Here are some ideas: 
 Personalised Photo Album: A collection of meaningful moments together. 
 Books: A favourite author's work or a book connected to her interests. 
 Flowers and a Handwritten Letter: A simple, personal gesture. 
 Traditional Outfit or Jewellery: A gift chosen according to her style. 
 Wellness or Hobby Experience: An activity she genuinely enjoys. 
 Shared Celebration: Preparing a meal or planning quality time together. 
 A thoughtful gift reflects care, understanding and appreciation rather than the price of the item.

 These are original greeting suggestions rather than quotations from religious texts. 
 How Can Families Celebrate Karwa Chauth Meaningfully? 
 Karwa Chauth is also an opportunity to spend time with loved ones and appreciate family traditions. 
 Families can make the occasion meaningful by: 
 Preparing festive food together before or after the observance. 
 Helping with puja arrangements and household responsibilities. 
 Learning the cultural significance of Sargi and Baya. 
 Sharing traditional Karwa Chauth stories with younger family members. 
 Decorating the home with diyas, flowers and rangoli. 
 Exchanging thoughtful wishes and expressing appreciation. 
 Respecting individual choices about fasting and participation. 
 The festival can be celebrated through kindness, companionship and meaningful family time, regardless of how elaborate the arrangements are. 
 Conclusion: Celebrating Karwa Chauth 2026 With Love and Tradition 
 Karwa Chauth 2026 falls on Thursday, 29 October , with the New Delhi Puja Muhurat scheduled from 5:38 PM to 6:56 PM and moonrise at 8:17 PM , according to Drik Panchang. 
 The festival brings together traditions such as Sargi, Vrat Katha, evening puja, Mehndi, Solah Shringar and moon-sighting rituals. Beyond these customs, Karwa Chauth represents affection, commitment, family relationships and cultural heritage. 
 Whether celebrating through prayer, exchanging gifts, sharing heartfelt messages or spending time together, the occasion is an opportunity to appreciate loved ones and respect family traditions. 
 Happy Karwa Chauth 2026! 
 FAQs on Karwa Chauth 2026: Date, Puja Muhurat, Moonrise Time, Katha and Wishes
 1. When is Karwa Chauth in 2026? 
 Karwa Chauth 2026 will be celebrated on Thursday, 29 October 2026 , in India. It falls on Krishna Paksha Chaturthi and is traditionally observed with fasting, prayers and moon-sighting rituals. 
 2. Is Karwa Chauth 2026 on 28 or 29 October? 
 Karwa Chauth is on 29 October 2026 , not 28 October, in India. According to Drik Panchang, Chaturthi Tithi begins at 1:06 AM and ends at 10:09 PM on 29 October. 
 3. What is the Karwa Chauth 2026 Puja Muhurat? 
 The Karwa Chauth 2026 Puja Muhurat in New Delhi is 5:38 PM to 6:56 PM , according to Drik Panchang. The timing differs by location. 
 4. What time will the moon rise on Karwa Chauth 2026? 
 Moonrise in New Delhi is calculated for 8:17 PM on 29 October 2026 . Other cities have different moonrise timings. 
 5. What is the Sargi time for Karwa Chauth 2026? 
 Sargi is traditionally eaten before sunrise. In New Delhi, sunrise and the fasting start time are 6:31 AM on 29 October 2026. Families should finish Sargi before sunrise according to their customs. 
 6. What is Karwa Chauth Katha? 
 Karwa Chauth Katha is a traditional religious story recited during the evening puja. One popular version tells the story of Queen Veeravati and her seven brothers. 
 7. What is the story of Queen Veeravati on Karwa Chauth? 
 According to tradition, Veeravati's brothers created a false moonlight appearance to persuade her to end her fast early. The story describes the difficulties that followed and her renewed devotion. 
 8. What items are needed for Karwa Chauth Puja? 
 Common Karwa Chauth Puja Samagri includes a Karwa, Puja Thali, diya, roli, rice, flowers, sweets, water, sieve and Vrat Katha book. Materials vary by family tradition. 
 9. How should Karwa Chauth Vrat be broken? 
 The fast is traditionally broken after sighting the moon, offering Arghya and completing the customary prayers. In many families, the husband then offers water and food to his wife. 
 10. Is Nirjala fasting compulsory on Karwa Chauth? 
 Nirjala fasting is a traditional practice, but not everyone observes the festival in the same way. Individuals should consider their health and seek medical advice when appropriate. 
 11. Which Mehndi designs are best for Karwa Chauth? 
 Popular styles include traditional full-hand Mehndi, floral patterns, mandalas, Arabic Mehndi and minimal finger designs. The best choice depends on personal preference and the time available. 
 12. What are some easy Mehndi designs for beginners on Karwa Chauth? 
 Beginners can try simple flowers, leafy vines, dotted mandalas, bracelet patterns or a single floral design on the palm. 
 13. What is a meaningful Karwa Chauth gift for your wife? 
 Thoughtful ideas include personalised gifts, books, flowers, jewellery, a handwritten letter or a shared experience based on her interests. 
 14. What are some good Karwa Chauth wishes? 
 You can say, "Happy Karwa Chauth! May your life be filled with love, trust and happiness." Personal messages expressing appreciation are especially meaningful. 
 15. What is the significance of Sargi and Baya on Karwa Chauth? 
 Sargi is the traditional pre-dawn meal, often given by the mother-in-law. Baya refers to gifts and offerings exchanged according to household customs, symbolising family relationships. 
 16. Why is the moon important on Karwa Chauth? 
 Moon sighting is central to the traditional fast-breaking ritual. Devotees offer Arghya to the moon and complete their prayers before ending the fast. 
 17. Is Karwa Chauth celebrated only in North India? 
 Karwa Chauth is especially popular in North India, but families living in other regions and countries also observe it according to their customs. 
 18. Can unmarried women celebrate Karwa Chauth? 
 Although Karwa Chauth is traditionally associated with married women, some unmarried women also choose to participate according to personal beliefs and family traditions.
